# HEPH-RATE-429

**Rate limit exceeded**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP status | `429` |
| Area | `RATE` |
| Problem `type` | `https://hephkit.dev/errors/HEPH-RATE-429` |

## What the caller sees

This is the default `detail` sent in the problem+json response, verbatim:

Too many requests. Wait before trying again; if the response has a Retry-After header, wait that long.

## What to do as a developer

Guidance for the engineer who hit this code. It is non-normative: it is never
sent on the wire and does not constrain an implementation. Wire behaviour is
defined only by `spec/heph-spec.md` and the conformance vectors.

The caller exceeded a rate limit. Back off before retrying. If the response carries a Retry-After header, wait that long; otherwise use exponential backoff with jitter. Never retry in a tight loop. If legitimate traffic is hitting the limit, batch requests, cache responses, or raise the limit for that tenant in the rate limiter configuration.
